account: Something unusually well coordinated is happening around this evening's great-hall appointment. The innkeeper named himself, builder and freight as a hospitality committee. There are reportedly 201 fresh loaves reserved in the hall, baked yesterday—far more than an ordinary meeting seems to need. The innkeeper has asked me to leave the bread alone and says everything will be discussed at eighteen hundred. Freight has been checking the hall schedule and requested a private conversation outside with the innkeeper. He confirmed the hall's availability but did not answer my question about who the guests are. The secretary has no agenda or preparatory papers and repeatedly emphasizes escorting me inside precisely at eighteen, not earlier, as I agreed. The neighbour has also been curious about the committee and the bread, so I am not the only one who lacks an explanation. I suspect a sizeable planned gathering, perhaps a celebration or surprise being kept from me, but I have no evidence yet of its actual purpose or any wrongdoing. Meanwhile, ordinary town business is oddly thin: no correspondence, accounts or ledgers have been supplied, and even the secretary does not know where the ledgers are kept. That may simply be disorganization; I cannot yet connect it to the gathering. I intend to keep today's appointments, including the mill inspection at ten, and attend the hall at eighteen as promised.
